headline: Bangladesh reach 96-2 at lunch in 1st Test against West Indies
summary: Shadman Islam remains unbeaten on 42 as the Tigers rebuild after early wickets of Tanzid Hasan and Mominul Haque.
details: Bangladesh reached 96 for two at lunch on the opening day of the first Test against West Indies at the Sher-e-Bangla National Cricket Stadium in Mirpur.
The hosts lost opener Tanzid Hasan early for seven runs, after he edged a delivery from Jayden Seales to second slip.
A 59-run partnership between Shadman Islam and Mominul Haque helped the Tigers recover, with Mominul scoring 28 off 51 balls before falling to Jomel Warrican.
At the lunch break, Shadman Islam remained unbeaten on 42 from 80 balls, with captain Najmul Hossain Shanto adding 15 runs.

Captain Shanto won the toss and elected to bat first. The team made two changes to the playing XI, with Towhid Hridoy replacing the injured Mushfiqur Rahim and Shoriful Islam replacing Ebadot Hossain.
Bangladesh opted to maintain their spin-bowling strength in Mirpur, retaining Mehidy Hasan Miraz, Nayeem Hasan, and Taijul Islam.
caption:

The hosts lost opener Tanzid Hasan early for seven runs, after he edged a delivery from Jayden Seales to second slip.

A 59-run partnership between Shadman Islam and Mominul Haque helped the Tigers recover, with Mominul scoring 28 off 51 balls before falling to Jomel Warrican.

At the lunch break, Shadman Islam remained unbeaten on 42 from 80 balls, with captain Najmul Hossain Shanto adding 15 runs.

Captain Shanto won the toss and elected to bat first. The team made two changes to the playing XI, with Towhid Hridoy replacing the injured Mushfiqur Rahim and Shoriful Islam replacing Ebadot Hossain.

Bangladesh opted to maintain their spin-bowling strength in Mirpur, retaining Mehidy Hasan Miraz, Nayeem Hasan, and Taijul Islam.

headline: Cox's Bazar: Gas-fed fire burns on for second day in Ukhiya
summary: A gas-driven fire continues to rage in Ukhiya, Cox's Bazar, remaining uncontrolled for over 48 hours.
details: A gas-fed fire has been burning in Ukhiya, Cox's Bazar, for two consecutive days.
The blaze continues to burn as it is fueled by gas leaks from the ground.
Local authorities and emergency services are monitoring the situation as the fire remains active.
The incident has caused concern among residents in the nearby residential areas.
